links.comparator_used: Same locally-deployed LLM (gpt-oss-20b) without RAG-based local guideline context, and a frontier model (gpt-5.4) without RAG
links.outcome: Proportion of answers to simulated antimicrobial advice questions judged fully correct
links.effect: With RAG, 162/186 (87%) attempted answers were fully correct. Without RAG, 21/186 (11%) were fully correct with the same local LLM and 92/200 (46%) with gpt-5.4.
links.tradeoff: RAG still produced occasional errors (5% incorrect, 8% partially correct), performance was lower in complex scenarios such as renal impairment, and only 5/9 (56%) out-of-scope questions were correctly identified. Median generation time was 12 s (single-stage).
links.quote: LLMs without RAG-based local guideline context had lower performance: 21/186 (11%) answers to simulated questions fully correct with the same locally-deployed LLM and 92/200 (46%) with a current frontier model (gpt-5.4).

design_hint: retrieval-augmented generation grounding on local clinical guidelines
